title: On Reward Functions for Self-Improving General-Purpose Reasoning (submitted as: Towards Learning to Reason at Pre-Training Scale)

contributions.purpose: Establish what makes a reward function suitable for self-improving Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning on unstructured pretraining-scale text, and expose why commonly used reward functions fail.
contributions.mechanism: Define desirable criteria for such reward functions; empirical analysis of how different reward functions affect 'what' reasoning is rewarded (distinguishing meaningful CoT from random word sequences) and 'where' reasoning is rewarded (picking useful locations vs. trivial next-token spots).
contributions.evaluation: Two experiments (Sections 5.1) show common rewards (standard loss, delta loss) fail: cannot differentiate meaningful CoT from random sequences and incentivize reasoning where prediction is trivial; RA best satisfies criteria in Table 1.
contributions.source_quote: We establish desirable criteria of reward functions for self-improving CoT reasoning on unstructured text at pretraining scale.

contributions.purpose: Provide a reward function that actually enables self-improving CoT reasoning on free-form QA where answers are unstructured and hard to verify.
contributions.mechanism: Introduce Reasoning Advantage (RA), a reward based on clipped normalized language-modeling loss (clipped delta loss normalized by an 'Empty CoT' baseline); used to filter synthetically generated CoTs in an iterative-SFT (RAFT-style) self-improvement loop.
contributions.evaluation: RA is the only reward function that facilitates self-improvement of CoT reasoning on MMLU-FREE-FORM; ablations show clipping is almost never harmful and the 'Empty CoT' baseline gives a substantial boost without extra CoT generation; RA is the only function strong on both 'what' and 'where' tasks.
contributions.source_quote: We propose Reasoning Advantage (RA), a novel reward function based on clipped normalized loss, and demonstrate that RA is the only reward function which facilitates self-improvement of CoT reasoning on MMLU-FREE-FORM

contributions.purpose: Provide an intermediate benchmark that enables efficient study of self-improving CoT reasoning between curated QA datasets and full unstructured pretraining text.
contributions.mechanism: Construct MMLU-FREE-FORM, an open-ended QA dataset derived toward the unstructured pretraining setting, designed to reveal limitations of commonly used reward functions.
contributions.evaluation: Serves as intermediate benchmark; used to show only RA generalizes when self-improving CoT reasoning; qualitative demonstration of reward-function failures.
contributions.source_quote: We introduce MMLU-FREE-FORM, an open-ended QA dataset that facilitates more efficient study of self-improving CoT reasoning and reveals the limitations of commonly used reward functions.

self_declared_provenance.quote: Havrilla et al. (2024a) show that Expert Iteration ... outperforms RL in their evaluations. Building on this, our work extends RAFT (Dong et al., 2023), which also uses iterative SFT, by introducing a new reward function called Reasoning Advantage (RA) for filtering synthetically generated CoTs.

This limitation is evident in the policy gradient objective approximated by STaR (Zelikman et al., 2022) ... which makes use of an indicator function with respect to ground truth labels. Clearly, this breaks down in settings where ground truth labels are not available (motivating RA's label-free reward).

notes: Rejected. Explicitly negative/honest exploratory result: the flagship pretraining-scale experiment on OpenWebMath FAILS - the offline RL procedure cannot escape a local optimum of extremely conservative CoT that just summarizes prior information instead of solving the problem; authors conclude future work must generate more diverse CoTs. Ablation caveat: two augmentation combinations and non-normalized RA did slightly better on 'what' experiments but much worse on 'where'; RA wins only by being balanced across both. Note: PDF title ('On Reward Functions for Self-Improving General-Purpose Reasoning') differs from the batch-listed title ('Towards Learning to Reason at Pre-Training Scale').
